newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS-Den Danske earnings slip in 1996.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Den Danske earnings slip in 1996.

text.p: Denmark's Den Danske Bank on Thursday published a 1996 annual report that initially confused the market, announcing better-than-forecast profits that were nevertheless down on the year before and growth in core earnings that it said it was unlikely to repeat.

The country's biggest bank revealed profits before tax and extraordinary items of 5.396 billion crowns ($838 million), lower than 1995's 6.034 billion crowns but better than analysts' average forecast of 4.800 billion crowns.
In a statement accompanying the report, chief executive Knud Soerensen expressed qualified satisfaction.
"The year's result is fairly satisfactory as far as I can see," he said.
Core earnings, heavily-boosted by a 617 million crown fall in bad debt provisions, rose to 3.73 billion crowns in 1996 from 2.785 billion the year before.
Insurance earnings rose with the inclusion of the Danica insurance unit, acquired in 1995, for the first full year.
But the bank acknowledged that many of 1996's fruits would not be harvested again in 1997.
"Expenses are not likely to fall in 1997 and it may not be possible to keep bad debt provisions at the low level seen in 1996," the report said.
"Core earnings seem unlikely to improve and therefore earnings will probably not be sufficent to ensure a fully satisfactory return on the group's considerable equity," it added.
The report went on to say that technological improvement and Nordic expansion precluded cost savings during the coming year.
"Despite tight cost controls, including staff reductions, the bank's costs are not expected to fall," it said.
Operating costs fell in 1996 to 5.7 billion crowns from 5.8 billion in 1995, giving an income/cost ratio of 1.71 times.
The bank shed 403 staff and closed six branches in 1996 and has said that it will lay off another 550 workers -- five percent of the workforce -- this year.
The announcement last month of the planned 1997 dismissals brought some staff stoppages, but so far no serious disruption.
The mixture of good and bad news sent the bank's share yo-yoing from 604 crowns just before the report was published at 1035 GMT, to a low of 589 crowns, then up to a high of 630 crowns.
At 1315 GMT it was trading at 624 crowns, up seven from Wednesday's close.

The report logged a rise in Den Danske's market share of total banking-sector lending to 33.5 percent from 32.4 percent and said that core earnings, including insurance, returned 16.5 percent on beginning-of-year equity of 23.1 billion crowns.
The dividend was to remain unchanged at 16 crowns per 100 crown share.
